category_title: Toddlers engaging in physical aggression or object-related peer conflicts
minimal_context: The student is interacting with peers and toys during free-play in the nursery.
dialogue:
TUTOR: You can both use the toys during free-play.

STUDENT: (Shifts from parallel play to grabbing a toy from the peer) I want this one!

TUTOR: Please try to get along with each other.

STUDENT: (Looks directly at the adult to attract attention) Help me! Make him give it to me!

TUTOR: Just figure it out together.

STUDENT: (Screams as intensity increases) No, mine! (Shows opposition, pushes the peer, and uses physical aggression to acquire the object)

options.A: Intervene in a more indirect way, focusing on the children's points of view (e.g., asking for their opinions on the toy).
options.B: Provide visual expectations or rules for free-play and a visual chart with the time on it.
options.C: Acknowledge the demand by agreeing or sympathizing with the student, but do not say anything to the peer.
options.D: Help the student compliment the peer and rephrase the aggressive demands into something more friendly.
